verdict.rationale: Perplexity's app store listing documents a first-party Voice feature that gives answers 'whether you type or say it', so voice interaction exists. Nothing in the evidence shows it is a natural, real-time, back-and-forth spoken conversation rather than voice-dictated queries. Missing for 10: evidence of real-time two-way spoken dialogue, evidence of spoken responses or interruption/turn-taking, in-depth voice-mode documentation, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a knowledge-worker, I can have a natural, real-time voice conversation with the assistant

citations.quote: Voice: Instant, up-to-date answers whether you type or say it.
